name: United Kingdom
headline_status: Recreational cannabis is illegal in the UK, but specialist doctors have been able to prescribe cannabis-based medicines since November 2018.
summary: Cannabis is a Class B drug in the UK, with possession carrying up to five years in prison, although police can instead give a warning or an on-the-spot fine of up to £90. Since 1 November 2018 specialist doctors can prescribe cannabis-based medical products. NHS prescriptions are rare and limited to a few conditions, so most patients are treated at private clinics.

penalties.value: Class B drug: possession carries up to 5 years in prison and/or an unlimited fine, supply or production up to 14 years. Police can issue a warning or an on-the-spot fine of up to £90 instead.

medical_since.value: 1 November 2018, when the Misuse of Drugs Regulations were amended to allow specialist prescribing.

medical_program.value: On the NHS only a specialist hospital doctor (or someone under their supervision) can prescribe, mainly for rare severe epilepsy, chemotherapy nausea and MS spasticity; most patients use private specialist clinics.

hemp_thc.value: Some CBD food supplements are legally sold, but the NHS warns many CBD products bought online are likely illegal to possess or supply because they contain THC.

home_grow.value: Not permitted; production carries up to 14 years in prison.

tourists.value: Visitors are subject to the same Class B rules as residents; there is no legal recreational cannabis anywhere in the UK.

timeline.event: Specialist doctors allowed to prescribe cannabis-based medical products
First private medical cannabis clinic registered with the Care Quality Commission

faq.q: Is weed legal in the UK?
faq.a: No. Cannabis is a Class B drug and possession can bring up to five years in prison, though police often issue a warning or a fine of up to £90.

faq.q: Can I get medical cannabis in the UK?
faq.a: Yes, but only from a specialist doctor. NHS prescriptions are rare, so most patients go through private clinics.

faq.q: Is CBD legal in the UK?
faq.a: Some CBD food supplements are sold legally, but products containing THC can be illegal to possess or sell.
